name: Bluish Slate-Black
lede: Bluish Slate-Black is a near-black green-blue from Ridgway's 1912 plates, and the swatch our library pairs with the Japanese word ai-iro, indigo color.

sections.title: A dark slate, and a Japanese pairing
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 standards place this swatch on plate XLVIII, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classes a close match as a dark blue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[greenish-slate-black]], [[black-green]], [[dark-slate-grey]] and [[dark-delft-blue]], at 3.1, 4.3, 4.4 and 4.4 ΔE [1]. Our library also files it next to the Japanese term 藍色, romanized Ai-iro and meaning indigo color, though the pairing is by hue proximity, not a translation [1].

A near-duplicate from the same Ridgway plate sits only 1.2 ΔE away: Dull Blue-Green Black [1]. The nearest everyday name on file is [[charcoal]], not far from [[denim]] and [[black-coral]] in the same dark, low-chroma corner of our library [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 431 of 23,781 paintings (1.81 percent), as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 45 of 1,674 paintings, at 2.9 times the archive's overall rate, is over-represented in paintings from Norway (4.0 times expected), and Paul Cezanne used it most, 5.4 times his museums' baseline [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, which fits a near-black color [2]. The earliest dated match, from 1099, predates the 1912 record by eight centuries, which the archive's thin early coverage makes a floor, not a first sighting of the actual name [2].
